title: Laws of indices
statement: Laws of indices for all rational exponents.
guidance: $a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}$, $a^m \div a^n = a^{m-n}$, $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$. The equivalence of $a^{\frac{1}{n}}$ and $\sqrt[n]{a}$, and of $a^{\frac{m}{n}}$ and $(\sqrt[n]{a})^m$, should be known.

title: Manipulating surds
statement: Use and manipulation of surds.
guidance: Students should be able to rationalise denominators.

title: Quadratic functions and graphs
statement: Quadratic functions and their graphs.

title: The discriminant
statement: The discriminant of a quadratic function.
guidance: Need to know and to use $b^2-4ac>0$, $b^2-4ac=0$ and $b^2-4ac<0$.

title: Solving quadratic equations
statement: Completing the square. Solution of quadratic equations.
guidance: Solution of quadratic equations by factorisation, use of the formula, use of a calculator and completing the square: $ax^2+bx+c = a\left(x+\dfrac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + c - \dfrac{b^2}{4a}$.

title: Simultaneous equations by substitution
statement: Solve simultaneous equations; analytical solution by substitution.

title: Interpreting inequalities graphically
statement: Interpret linear and quadratic inequalities graphically.
guidance: For example, $ax+b>cx+d$, $px^2+qx+r \geq 0$, $px^2+qx+r<ax+b$. Interpreting the third inequality as the range of $x$ for which the curve $y=px^2+qx+r$ is below the line with equation $y=ax+b$. Including inequalities with brackets and fractions; these are reducible to linear or quadratic inequalities, e.g. $\dfrac{a}{x}<b$ becomes $ax<bx^2$, $x \neq 0$.

title: Graphing inequality regions
statement: Represent linear and quadratic inequalities graphically.
guidance: Represent linear and quadratic inequalities such as $y>x+r$ and $y>ax^2+bx+c$ graphically. Shading and use of dotted and solid line convention is required.

title: Solving linear and quadratic inequalities
statement: Solutions of linear and quadratic inequalities.
guidance: For example, solving $ax+b>cx+d$, $px^2+qx+r \geq 0$, $px^2+qx+r<ax+b$.

title: Manipulating and factorising polynomials
statement: Algebraic manipulation of polynomials, including expanding brackets and collecting like terms, factorisation.
guidance: Students should be able to expand brackets and collect like terms. Factorisation of polynomials of degree $n$, $n \leq 3$, e.g. $x^3+4x^2+3x$. The notation $f(x)$ may be used.

title: Sketching curves and using intersections
statement: Graphs of functions; sketching curves defined by simple equations. Geometrical interpretation of algebraic solution of equations. Use of intersection points of graphs of functions to solve equations.
guidance: Functions to include simple cubic functions and the reciprocal functions $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$ and $y=\dfrac{k}{x^2}$ with $x \neq 0$. Knowledge of the term asymptote is expected. Also, trigonometric graphs.

title: Graph transformations
statement: Knowledge of the effect of simple transformations on the graph of $y=f(x)$ as represented by $y=af(x)$, $y=f(x)+a$, $y=f(x+a)$, $y=f(ax)$.
guidance: Students should be able to apply one of these transformations to any of the above functions (quadratics, cubics, reciprocals, sine, cosine, and tangent) and sketch the resulting graphs. Given the graph of any function $y=f(x)$, students should be able to sketch the graph resulting from one of these transformations.

title: Equations of straight lines
statement: Equation of a straight line, including the forms $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$ and $ax+by+c=0$.
guidance: To include: (i) the equation of a line through two given points; (ii) the equation of a line parallel (or perpendicular) to a given line through a given point. For example, the line perpendicular to the line $3x+4y=18$ through the point $(2,3)$ has equation $y-3=\dfrac{4}{3}(x-2)$.

title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
statement: Conditions for two straight lines to be parallel or perpendicular to each other.

title: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area
statement: The sine and cosine rules, and the area of a triangle in the form $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
guidance: Including the ambiguous case of the sine rule.

title: Radians, arc length and sector area
statement: Radian measure, including use for arc length and area of sector.
guidance: Use of the formulae $s=r\theta$ and $A=\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$.

title: Trig function graphs and periodicity
statement: Sine, cosine and tangent functions. Their graphs, symmetries and periodicity.
guidance: Knowledge of graphs of curves with equations such as $y=3\sin x$, $y=\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$, $y=\sin 2x$ is expected.

title: Derivative as gradient and rate of change
statement: The derivative of $f(x)$ as the gradient of the tangent to the graph of $y=f(x)$ at a point; the gradient of the tangent as a limit; interpretation as a rate of change; second order derivatives.
guidance: For example, knowledge that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is the rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$. Knowledge of the chain rule is not required. The notation $f'(x)$ and $f''(x)$ may be used.

title: Differentiating powers of x
statement: Differentiation of $x^n$, and related sums, differences and constant multiples.
guidance: The ability to differentiate expressions such as $(2x+5)(x-1)$ and $\dfrac{2x^2+5x-3}{3x}$ is expected.

title: Tangents and normals
statement: Applications of differentiation to gradients, tangents and normals.
guidance: Use of differentiation to find equations of tangents and normals at specific points on a curve.

title: Integration as reverse of differentiation
statement: Indefinite integration as the reverse of differentiation.
guidance: Students should know that a constant of integration is required.

title: Integrating powers of x
statement: Integration of $x^n$ and related sums, differences and constant multiples.
guidance: (Excluding $n=-1$, and related sums, differences and multiples). For example, the ability to integrate expressions such as $(x+2)^2$ and $\dfrac{3x-1}{2x^2}$ is expected. Given $f'(x)$ and a point on the curve, students should be able to find an equation of the curve in the form $y=f(x)$.

title: Structure of mathematical proof
statement: Understand and use the structure of mathematical proof, proceeding from given assumptions through a series of logical steps to a conclusion; use methods of proof stated below:

title: Proof by exhaustion
statement: Proof by exhaustion
guidance: Proof by exhaustion. This involves trying all the options. Suppose $x$ and $y$ are odd integers less than 7. Prove that their sum is divisible by 2.

title: Disproof by counterexample
statement: Disproof by counter example.
guidance: Disproof by counter example – show that the statement “$n^2-n+1$ is a prime number for all values of $n$” is untrue.

title: Factor and remainder theorems
statement: Simple algebraic division; use of the Factor Theorem and the Remainder Theorem.
guidance: Only division by $(ax+b)$ or $(ax-b)$ will be required, e.g. students should know that if $f(x)=0$ when $x=\dfrac{b}{a}$, then $(ax-b)$ is a factor of $f(x)$. Students may be required to factorise cubic expressions such as $x^3+3x^2-4$ and $6x^3+11x^2-x-6$. Students should be familiar with the terms 'quotient' and 'remainder' and be able to determine the remainder when the polynomial $f(x)$ is divided by $(ax+b)$.

title: Equation and properties of a circle
statement: Coordinate geometry of the circle using the equation of a circle in the form $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$ and including use of the following circle properties: (i) the angle in a semicircle is a right angle; (ii) the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord; (iii) the perpendicularity of radius and tangent.
guidance: Students should be able to find the radius and the coordinates of the centre of the circle, given the equation of the circle and vice versa.

title: Sequences and recurrence relations
statement: Sequences, including those given by a formula for the $n$th term and those generated by a simple relation of the form $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$.

title: Arithmetic sequences and series
statement: Understand and work with arithmetic sequences and series, including the formula for the nth term and the sum of a finite arithmetic series; the sum of the first n natural numbers.
guidance: The proof of the sum formula should be known. Understanding of $\Sigma$ notation will be expected.

title: Increasing, decreasing and periodic sequences
statement: Increasing sequences, decreasing sequences and periodic sequences.

title: Geometric sequences and series
statement: Understand and work with geometric sequences and series, including the formulae for the $n$th term and the sum of a finite geometric series; the sum to infinity of a convergent geometric series, including the use of $|r|<1$. Binomial expansion of $(a+bx)^n$ for
guidance: For example, given the sum of a series students should be able to use logarithms to find the value of $n$. The proof of the sum formula for a finite series should be known. The sum to infinity may be expressed as $S_\infty$.

title: Binomial expansion for positive integer n
statement: positive integer $n$.
guidance: The notations $n!$, $\dbinom{n}{r}$ and ${}^nC_r$ may be used.

title: Exponential function y = a^x
statement: $y=a^x$ and its graph.

title: Laws of logarithms
statement: Laws of logarithms.
guidance: To include $\log_a(xy) \equiv \log_a x + \log_a y$, $\log_a\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) \equiv \log_a x - \log_a y$, $\log_a(x^k) \equiv k\log_a x$, $\log_a\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) \equiv -\log_a x$, $\log_a a = 1$, where $a,x,y>0$, $a \neq 1$.

title: Solving a^x = b
statement: The solution of equations of the form $a^x=b$.
guidance: Students may use the change of base formula.

title: Trigonometric identities tan and Pythagorean
statement: Knowledge and use of $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$.

title: Solving trigonometric equations
statement: Solution of simple trigonometric equations in a given interval.
guidance: Students should be able to solve equations such as $\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=\dfrac{3}{4}$ for $0<x<2\pi$, $\cos(x+30^{\circ})=\dfrac{1}{2}$ for $-180^{\circ}<x<180^{\circ}$, $\tan 2x=1$ for $90^{\circ}<x<270^{\circ}$, $6\cos^2 x+\sin x-5=0$ for $0 \leq x<360^{\circ}$, $\sin\left(2x+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$ for $-\pi \leq x<\pi$.

title: Maxima, minima and stationary points
statement: Applications of differentiation to maxima and minima and stationary points, increasing and decreasing functions.
guidance: To include applications to curve sketching. Maxima and minima problems may be set in the context of a practical problem.

title: Evaluating definite integrals
statement: Evaluation of definite integrals.

title: Area under a curve
statement: Interpretation of the definite integral as the area under a curve.
guidance: Students will be expected to evaluate the area of a region bounded by a curve and given straight lines. For example, find the finite area bounded by the curve $y=6x-x^2$ and the line $y=2x$. $\int x \, dy$ will not be required. Students will be expected to be able to evaluate the area of a region bounded by two curves.

title: Trapezium rule
statement: Approximation of area under a curve using the trapezium rule.
guidance: For example, use the trapezium rule to approximate $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \sqrt{2x+1}\,dx$ using four strips. Use of an increasing number of trapezia to improve accuracy, and an estimate of the error, may be required.

title: Simplifying rational expressions
statement: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising and cancelling, and algebraic division.
guidance: Denominators of rational expressions will be linear or quadratic, e.g. $\dfrac{1}{ax+b}$, $\dfrac{x^3+1}{px^2+qx+r}$, $\dfrac{x-1}{x^2}$.

title: Functions, domain, range and inverses
statement: Definition of a function. Domain and range of functions. Composition of functions. Inverse functions and their graphs.
guidance: The concept of a function as a one-one or many-one mapping from $\mathbb{R}$ (or a subset of $\mathbb{R}$) to $\mathbb{R}$ will be used. The notation $f:x \mapsto f(x)$ may be used. Students should know that $fg$ means 'do $g$ first, then $f$'. Students should know that if $f^{-1}$ exists, then $f^{-1}f(x) = ff^{-1}(x) = x$.

title: The modulus function
statement: The modulus function.
guidance: Students should be able to sketch the graphs of $y=|ax+b|$ and the graphs of $y=|f(x)|$ and $y=f(|x|)$, given the graph of $y=f(x)$. For example, sketch the graph with equation $y=|2x-1|$ and use the graph to solve the equation $|2x-1|=x+5$ or the inequality $|2x-1|>x+5$.

title: Combined graph transformations
statement: Combinations of the transformations $y=f(x)$ as represented by $y=af(x)$, $y=f(x)+a$, $y=f(x+a)$, $y=f(ax)$.
guidance: Students should be able to sketch the graph of, for example, $y=2f(3x)$, $y=f(-x)+1$, given the graph of $y=f(x)$, or the graph of, for example, $y=3+\sin 2x$, $y=-\cos\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$. The graph of $y=f(ax+b)$ will not be required.

title: Reciprocal and inverse trig functions
statement: Knowledge of secant, cosecant and cotangent and of arcsin, arccos and arctan. Their relationships to sine, cosine and tangent. Understanding of their graphs and appropriate restricted domains.
guidance: Angles measured in both degrees and radians.

title: Sec² and cosec² identities
statement: Knowledge and use of $\sec^2\theta = 1+\tan^2\theta$ and $\csc^2\theta = 1+\cot^2\theta$.

title: Compound and double angle formulae
statement: Knowledge and use of double angle formulae; use of formulae for $\sin(A \pm B)$, $\cos(A \pm B)$ and $\tan(A \pm B)$ and of expressions for $a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta$ in the equivalent forms of $r\cos(\theta \pm \alpha)$ or $r\sin(\theta \pm \alpha)$.
guidance: To include application to half angles. Knowledge of the $t=\tan\frac{1}{2}\theta$ formulae will not be required. Students should be able to solve equations such as $a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta=c$ in a given interval, and to prove identities such as $\cos x\cos 2x+\sin x\sin 2x \equiv \cos x$.

title: The exponential function e^x
statement: The function $e^x$ and its graph.
guidance: To include the graph of $y=e^{ax+b}+c$. Solution of equations of the form $e^{ax+b}=p$ and

title: The natural logarithm ln x
statement: The function $\ln x$ and its graph; $\ln x$ as the inverse function of $e^x$.
guidance: $\ln(ax+b)=q$ is expected.

title: Using logarithmic graphs to fit models
statement: Use logarithmic graphs to estimate parameters in relationships of the form $y=ax^n$ and $y=kb^x$.
guidance: Plot $\log y$ against $\log x$ and obtain a straight line where the intercept is $\log a$ and the gradient is $n$. Plot $\log y$ against $x$ and obtain a straight line where the intercept is $\log k$ and the gradient is $\log b$.

title: Differentiating exponential, log and trig functions
statement: Differentiation of $e^{kx}$, $\ln kx$, $\sin kx$, $\cos kx$, $\tan kx$ and their sums and differences.

title: Product, quotient and chain rules
statement: Differentiation using the product rule, the quotient rule and the chain rule.
guidance: Differentiation of $\csc x$, $\cot x$ and $\sec x$ is required. Skill will be expected in the differentiation of functions generated from standard functions using products, quotients and composition, such as $3e^x\sin x$, $\dfrac{2x^4}{\cos x}$, $\cos(x^2)$ and $\tan^2 2x$.

title: Differentiating using dy/dx = 1/(dx/dy)
statement: The use of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{dx/dy}$.
guidance: For example, finding $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ for $x=\sin 3y$.

title: Exponential growth and decay
statement: Understand and use exponential growth and decay.
guidance: Students should be familiar with terms such as 'initial', meaning when $t=0$. Students may need to explore the behaviour for large values of $t$ or to consider whether the range of values predicted is appropriate. Consideration of a second, improved model may be required. Knowledge and use of the result $\dfrac{d}{dx}(a^x) = a^x \ln a$ is expected.

title: Integrating exponential, log and trig functions
statement: Integration of $e^{kx}$, $\dfrac{1}{nx}$, $\sin kx$, $\cos kx$ and their sums and differences.
guidance: To include integration of standard functions such as $\sin 3x$, $e^{5x}$, $\dfrac{1}{2x}$.

title: Integration by recognition
statement: Integration by recognition of known derivatives to include integrals of the form $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)|+c$ and $\displaystyle\int f'(x)[f(x)]^n\,dx = \dfrac{[f(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1}+c$.
guidance: For example, to include integration of $\tan x$, $\sec^2 2x$. Students are expected to be able to use trigonometric identities to integrate, for example, $\sin^2 x$, $\tan^2 x$, $\cos^2 3x$.

title: Locating roots by sign change
statement: Location of roots of $f(x) = 0$ by considering changes of sign of $f(x)$ in an interval of $x$ in which $f(x)$ is continuous.

title: Iterative methods for equations
statement: Approximate solution of equations using simple iterative methods, including recurrence relations of the form $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$.
guidance: Solution of equations by use of iterative procedures, for which leads will be given.

title: Proof by contradiction
statement: Proof by contradiction
guidance: Including proof of the irrationality of $\sqrt{2}$ and the infinity of primes, and application to unfamiliar proofs.

title: Partial fractions
statement: Decompose rational functions into partial fractions (denominators not more complicated than repeated linear terms).
guidance: Partial fractions to include denominators such as $(ax+b)(cx+d)(ex+f)$ and $(ax+b)(cx+d)^2$. The degree of the numerator may equal or exceed the degree of the denominator. Applications to integration, differentiation and series expansions. Quadratic factors in the denominator such as $(x^2+a)$, $a>0$, are not required.

title: Parametric equations of curves
statement: Parametric equations of curves and conversion between cartesian and parametric forms.

title: Binomial series for rational n
statement: Binomial Series for any rational $n$.
guidance: For $|x| < \dfrac{b}{a}$, students should be able to obtain the expansion of $(ax+b)^n$, and the expansion of rational functions by decomposition into partial fractions.

title: Implicit and parametric differentiation
statement: Differentiation of simple functions defined implicitly or parametrically.
guidance: The finding of equations of tangents and normals to curves given parametrically or implicitly is required.

title: Forming differential equations
statement: Formation of simple differential equations.
guidance: Questions involving connected rates of change may be set.

title: Volume of revolution
statement: Evaluation of volume of revolution.
guidance: $\pi\displaystyle\int y^2\,dx$ is required, but not $\pi\displaystyle\int x^2\,dy$. Students should be able to find a volume of revolution, given parametric equations.

title: Integration by substitution and by parts
statement: Simple cases of integration by substitution and integration by parts. Understand these methods as the reverse processes of the chain and product rules respectively.
guidance: Students will be expected to use a substitution to find, e.g. $\displaystyle\int x\sqrt{x-2}\,dx$. The substitution will be given in more complicated integrals. The integral $\displaystyle\int \ln x\,dx$ is required. More than one application of integration by parts may be required, for example, $\displaystyle\int x^2 e^x\,dx$, $\displaystyle\int e^x \sin x\,dx$.

title: Integration using partial fractions
statement: Simple cases of integration using partial fractions.
guidance: Integration of rational expressions such as those arising from partial fractions, e.g. $\dfrac{3}{(x-1)^2}$, $\dfrac{2}{3x+5}$. Note that the integration of other rational expressions, such as $\dfrac{2x}{(2x-1)^4}$ and $\dfrac{5}{4x+2}$, is also required (see P3 section 5.2).

title: Separable differential equations
statement: Analytical solution of simple first order differential equations with separable variables.
guidance: General and particular solutions will be required.

title: Area under a parametric curve
statement: Use integration to find the area under a curve given its parametric equations.
guidance: Students should be able to find the area under a curve given its parametric equations. Students will not be expected to sketch a curve from its parametric equations.

title: Vectors in 2D and 3D
statement: Vectors in two and three dimensions.

title: Magnitude and unit vectors
statement: Magnitude of a vector.
guidance: Students should be able to find a unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf{a}$, and be familiar with $|\mathbf{a}|$.

title: Vector addition and scalar multiples
statement: Algebraic operations of vector addition and multiplication by scalars, and their geometrical interpretations.

title: Position vectors
statement: Position vectors.
guidance: $\overrightarrow{OB} - \overrightarrow{OA} = \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}$.

title: Distance between two points in 3D
statement: The distance between two points.
guidance: The distance $d$ between two points $(x_1,y_1,z_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2,z_2)$ is given by $d^2=(x_1-x_2)^2+(y_1-y_2)^2+(z_1-z_2)^2$.

title: Vector equations of lines
statement: Vector equations of lines.
guidance: To include the forms $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{a}+t\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{c}+t(\mathbf{d}-\mathbf{c})$. Conditions for two lines to be parallel, intersecting or skew.

title: Scalar product and angle between lines
statement: The scalar product. Its use for calculating the angle between two lines.
guidance: Students should know that for $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{a}=a_1\mathbf{i}+a_2\mathbf{j}+a_3\mathbf{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf{b}=b_1\mathbf{i}+b_2\mathbf{j}+b_3\mathbf{k}$, then $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}=a_1b_1+a_2b_2+a_3b_3$ and $\cos\angle AOB = \dfrac{\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}}{|\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|}$. Students should know that if $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}=0$, and $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are non-zero vectors, then $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are perpendicular.
